subject: Post-call: Lighthouse Analytics — topology & SLO alignment
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire@lighthouse.ai>, Devon Park <devon@lighthouse.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-27T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — Lighthouse Analytics / Redwood (latency & topology highlights)

Hi Claire / Devon —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned and can move towards a technical deep-dive next week: 

What we heard (pain + goals):
- Primary pain: unpredictable inference latency during peak batch scoring for real-time analytics (slower tail on complex prompts, spikes during daily batch window).
- Goal: sub-200ms P95 response for short prompts (avg ~120 tokens) during interactive queries, and predictable throughput for nightly batch scoring (target 6–8k reqs/min).
- Compliance: need SOC 2 + VPC/private deployment option for customer PII.

Key constraints / context you shared:
- Model: currently evaluating large open LLMs (baseline: Llama-2 family, 30–70B) and exploring 4-bit quantized variants for cost.
- Typical request profile: 60% short queries (<=150 tokens), 30% mid (150–600 tokens), 10% long (600–2k tokens). Peak concurrency observed: ~220 concurrent interactive sessions, batch window peaks add another ~400 concurrent workers.
- Integration: existing platform runs on GCP us-central, single-region production; would prefer Redwood Private in a VPC for initial rollout.

Recommended immediate next steps (we suggested on the call):
1) Schedule 60–90m technical deep-dive with your infra and ML engineering teams (Jordan & Irene to join on our side).
2) Lighthouse to share a 48-hour sample of request telemetry (anonymized) and 10 representative prompts for eval.
3) We’ll run a quick capacity sketch and propose a reference topology (hosted + dedicated reserved capacity / private VPC options) within 3 business days.

Attachments: I uploaded a mutual action plan and call recording for your notes (see attachments).

Open questions from us:
- Are there any hard latency SLOs for long-context requests, or are the SLOs only for short/mid queries?
- Do you expect multi-region failover or single-region with DR plan?

If that looks right, I’ll book the deep-dive for next Tue/Wed — what times work?

Thanks —
Mateo
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Mateo —

Thanks for the clear summary, that matches our understanding. A few clarifications: 

- Short/mid SLOs: target is P95 < 200ms for queries <= 200 tokens; for long-context (>= 600 tokens) we’re okay with relaxed SLOs (P95 < 1.2s) as long as throughput is predictable during batch windows.
- Multi-region: short-term single-region (us-central) is fine; long-term we want cross-region failover but that’s phase 2.
- Compliance: SOC2 required within onboarding (we’ll need your SOC2 report and details on private deployment timeline).

We’ll share the 48-hour telemetry export and 10 prompts by EOD Friday. Available for a deep-dive: Tue 2028-05-30 10:00–11:30 PDT or Wed 2028-05-31 13:00–14:30 PDT — either works for our infra team.

Look forward to the capacity sketch.

Best,
Claire Huang
Head of Platform Engineering | Lighthouse Analytics

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire@lighthouse.ai>, Devon Park <devon@lighthouse.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-28T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Lighthouse Analytics / Redwood (latency & topology highlights) — tech sketch attached

Claire / Devon —

Appreciate the clarifications. Per your availability we’ve penciled Tue 2028-05-30 10:30 PDT for the technical deep-dive (calendar invite to follow). Jordan and Irene will lead the topology discussion.

Quick engineering sketch / assumptions (pre-deep-dive):
- Request profile (from your notes): average tokens/request = 210, traffic mix short:mid:long = 60:30:10, peak combined concurrency (interactive + batch) = ~620.
- Latency SLOs to design to: interactive P95 <= 200ms for <= 200 tokens; degraded SLOs for long queries (P95 <= 1.2s). These drive different execution paths.

Reference topology (proposal):
1) Private VPC deployment (phase 1) — single-region us-central with dedicated GPU pool:
   - Dedicated nodes: 6x GPU workers (A100 80GB or equivalent) for hot-path interactive requests (supports low-latency variants of 30–70B models using q4_0 / q3_k quantization).
   - Batch pool: separate autoscaling group (spot/evictable for cost) sized to handle bursty nightly scoring (target capacity for peak: additional 8–10 GPUs for throughput).
   - Router & cache layer: request router with prefix KV cache + LRU for recent embeddings to cut average token compute; enable continuous batching for batch window jobs.

2) Model topology & serving variants:
   - Primary: quantized 30B model for interactive (q4_0, tuned kernels) — best latency/cost balance; target single-token decode p95 ~4–6ms on A100 optimized path.
   - Fallback: 70B quantized variant (q5_0) for quality-critical queries — routed based on policy, with higher cost and higher latency.
   - Caching: hot prefix caching for frequent prompts; KV-cache-backed reuse where applicable to reduce repeated prefix compute.

3) Autoscaling & routing policy:
   - Predictive scaling for nightly batch window based on historical telemetry (we’ll snap the 48-hr export into a capacity model).
   - Latency-preserving routing: prefer interactive pool for short requests; if load exceeds p95 cost target, degrade to small-quantized models rather than failing.

Capacity estimate (ballpark — will refine after telemetry):
- Interactive pool (6 GPUs A100 80GB): supports ~280–350 concurrent short queries with P95 ~<200ms (assumes batching disabled for latency-sensitive path).
- Batch pool (8 GPUs): supports sustained throughput ~10–12k reqs/min for mid-size payloads via batching (seq len ~500).

Security & compliance notes:
- Private deployment in your VPC + customer KMS recommended for PII requirements.
- We’ll provide SOC 2 report and network diagrams ahead of provisioning; compliance onboarding typically ~3–4 weeks after contract signature (depends on audit windows).

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Claire: share telemetry + prompts (ETA: 2028-05-31) — owner: Lighthouse.
- Mateo/Jordan/Irene: capacity sketch + topology diagram (ETA: 2028-06-03) — owner: Redwood SEs.
- Legal/Procurement: exchange MSA and initial SOW draft after mutual action plan sign-off — target week of 2028-06-10.

Attachments: initial topology sketch (outlined in the mutual action plan) and call recording.

If you have any constraints on GPU types or procurement windows, flag them before the deep-dive and we’ll incorporate. See you Tue 10:30 PDT.

Thanks —
Mateo Alvarez
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
